prompt:
# Guillaume, 2026-09-30 — stateloom as a system (two messages, verbatim)

Context: the proposal page "Stateloom Systems" (https://claude.ai/artifact/4arp9XZtSvyCvM6VwQD9NV) proposed a system document joining ERDF, SMDF and a new sequence document, with decisions D1–D9, questions Q1–Q5 and build steps A1–A13 across jgwill/smcraft, jgwill/Miadi, jgwill/medicine-wheel, jgwill/miadi-orchestration-kit, jgwill/llms-txt and miadi-review.

## Message 1

This is good work. When I look at your question number two Obviously, the design was done as I was progressing and creating the trading system, and it has not really been upgraded in relation to what was actually implemented. But what I'm getting from what you found is that we are going to be capable of finding contradictions or things that doesn't work inside of the system, which is great. And somehow I don't think we have to act on that strategy itself. For your question number three, I don't think we have to work on that either. And for the rest of most of what I've read so far is really great. Uh, in terms of the decision for the decision number one it makes sense for decision number two I agree with your recommendations to narrow with a rule with a subfolder and for decision number three I'm not sure we need to work on a branch. Nobody's using the service or whatever is running on the machine on the main branch. So I guess that you could actually start creating the, the sequence spec and the actual implementation that is sufficient to work and do these diagrams. And I really love the actual explanation that you that you made of where the sequence diagram is going to fit and how it relates to the entities and the state diagrams. What I'm getting is your scenario, which you translate to a sequence, needs to travel through all of the state machines that are there. So when you describe your scenario, it needs to fit in each of the state machine in each of the transitions. So it's pretty much two ways to tell the same stories, but it's really going to be powerful to use all of that with agents and probably also, you know, if we're designing a, a sequence diagram and it's part of the same system, it's going to be easy for us to implement some code that is going to do the validation in relationship to what is being designed in one diagram with the agent. So the agent creates something on the diagram and then he runs something and then it tells him we're going to upgrade also the state machine. So when the human goes to see the state machine diagram, it will have been upgraded according to the design that was actually in progress. In the sequence diagram because the scenario could also enable us to do multiple what I'm pointing at here is, is it's going to be possible to do multiple editing of multiple diagrams on the canvas surface so it's going to be, be a really amazing work to do so I'll let you start the work and if you need that would be good to actually use sub agents specialists as you progress to help you more make your work even more solid and I'm tempted to tell you to do all of the other packages upgrades and publishing that are needed they seem simple

## Message 2 (mid-work steering)

I hope I did not stop you. I wanted to steer something. And that was as simply as, yes, it could propose something, but you do, you need not to bore the user with a bunch of things he needs to approve and validate and all of these things. So there might be two modes here, which one is going to be free. It means that the sequence diagram, when we design it, if it implies some changes on the state machine or on the entity relationship diagram, the agent is going to be capable of doing them without validation. So there was going to be a need to be a modality that we can use to make this happen that way.  sir of a YOLO mode hahaha

ambiguities.text: "somehow I don't think we have to act on that strategy itself" (Q2)
ambiguities.suggestion: Close Q2 as no action on the trading system. Keep cross-diagram contradiction detection as a feature, and use the trading system only as test input if useful.

ambiguities.text: "I'm not sure we need to work on a branch"
ambiguities.suggestion: Treat as D3 resolved to main, based on the stated fact that nothing on this host depends on main. Verify running services before the first push.

ambiguities.text: "the actual implementation that is sufficient to work and do these diagrams"
ambiguities.suggestion: Set the minimum as: SQDF spec, protocol types and parser, Mermaid rendering, canvas rendering, cross-validation against state machines, and MCP tools. State anything left out.

ambiguities.text: "it's going to be easy for us to implement some code that is going to do the validation"
ambiguities.suggestion: Decide whether validation and propagation belong in this pass or the next one. The mid-work steering toward free mode suggests propagation is expected now.

ambiguities.text: "it's going to be possible to do multiple editing of multiple diagrams on the canvas surface"
ambiguities.suggestion: Record it as a later outcome in the system spec rather than building it in this pass.

ambiguities.text: "I'm tempted to tell you to do all of the other packages upgrades and publishing that are needed"
ambiguities.suggestion: Read it as permission to publish smcraft packages after tests pass. Treat cross-repo changes to repos with other owners (medicine-wheel, orchestration-kit, llms-txt, miadi-review) as separate outward acts and report each one.

ambiguities.text: "there might be two modes here, which one is going to be free" and "sir of a YOLO mode"
ambiguities.suggestion: The name of the mode and its default are Guillaume's to choose. Implement it with a neutral name (for example mode: propose | apply), make free mode available without an approval prompt, and bring the naming back to him.

ambiguities.text: "the agent is going to be capable of doing them without validation"
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify whether free mode skips human approval only or also skips automated schema checks. The safer reading keeps automated checks and a change log while removing the human prompt.

ambiguities.text: "if you need that would be good to actually use sub agents specialists"
ambiguities.suggestion: Use subagents for review and cross-repo steps, after the survey required by dispatch discipline.
